questions.q: What is the actual fix on the Territory page's headline card?
options: Remove [Total Sales (All Territories)] from the Values well and drag in the plain [Total Sales] measure instead
Rewrite the CALCULATE formula inside the benchmark measure
Delete DimTerritory and rebuild the relationship
Delete [Total Sales (All Territories)] entirely
questions.explain: Since Lesson 14 confirmed a binding mistake, the fix is a rebinding, not a DAX rewrite.

questions.q: Why does Total Sales (All Territories) stay in the model unchanged after the fix?
options: Its DAX is still correct and it's still needed as the denominator inside Pct of Company Total (Territory)
Power BI doesn't allow deleting measures
It no longer has any purpose but is kept for historical reasons
It must be deleted, but the lesson forgot to mention that
questions.explain: The measure itself was never the problem -- only which visual used it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson also recheck the Segment page, not just the Territory page?
options: The Segment page shares the same model and the same measure-naming risk (Total Sales All Segments)
The Segment page was rebuilt from scratch in this lesson
The Segment page has no relevant measures to check
Checking the Segment page is unrelated to this bug
questions.explain: The same kind of mis-binding risk could exist on the other page, so it's worth validating too.

questions.q: Why is renaming Total Sales (All Territories) safe?
options: Power BI Desktop updates every reference to a renamed measure automatically, including inside Pct of Company Total (Territory)'s formula
Renaming breaks every formula that references it, requiring manual fixes
Renaming only works if the measure has zero dependents
DAX measures cannot be renamed once created
questions.explain: References are by object, not typed text, so renaming propagates automatically.

questions.q: Why is validating against every territory more thorough than validating against only the one reported?
options: The earlier mistake was invisible with no filter applied, so testing only one case (or the unfiltered state) could hide a new problem the same way
Power BI requires testing every row before publishing
Testing one territory is always sufficient and this is just extra caution
Different territories use different measures entirely
questions.explain: A fix tested the same narrow way the bug was first missed could reintroduce or hide a related issue.
